text:
- chief complaint: right ankle pain after a fall the previous day.
- history of present illness: the patient slipped on ice and felt a pop, initially could not bear weight, and is now limping with partial weight-bearing. Icing, elevation, and ibuprofen have helped. Pain is 6/10 without ibuprofen and 1/10 with it. No prior ankle injury to this side.
- physical examination: bruising and swelling over the lateral malleolus, tenderness over the anterior lateral soft tissue, no laxity on anterior drawer or inversion stress, no bony tenderness, normal neurovascular exam. X-ray showed no fracture.
- symptoms experienced by the patient: right ankle pain, swelling, bruising, limping, difficulty bearing weight. No numbness or tingling.
- new medications prescribed or changed, including dosages: N/A. Ibuprofen continued as needed for pain and inflammation; dosage not provided.
- follow-up instructions: keep leg elevated when seated and continue icing. Use an air cast and crutches, stay off the leg for now, and begin weight-bearing as tolerated in a couple of days. Return in 14 days.
